newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies tumble to close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies tumble to close sharply lower.

text.p: CME pork belly futures tumbled from midsession gains to close sharply lower in a holiday shortened session. Hog futures also slipped to close mixed.
Pork bellies ended 2.325 cents lower to 0.950 higher with only distant August holding a gain. February finished 2.250 lower at 72.225 cents.

Early spillover strength from hog futures lacked followthrough and profit taking took pork bellies down into sell stops. Local long liquidation added to losses at the close to push prices down to day's lows. Technical pressure came despite strong fundamentals, traders said.

The reduced pace of hog slaughter, lighter than expected storings and higher cash product lent early support. Cash belly prices rose to $64 per cwt on Friday, the highest price level since October 14, they said.

Lind-Waldock and R.J. O'Brien sold late into sell stops. E.D. & F. Man sold early while Rand Financials and Saul Stone bought on the early advance. Locals turned sellers when hog futures retreated from early gains, pit sources said.
Hog futures also came under profit-taking pressure after recent gains, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.425 cent higher to 0.275 lower with December up most at 57.925 cents. December rallied to 58.525 early, its highest level since October 3rd when it posted a contract high of 58.800 cents.

Expectations of stronger cash hog markets Tuesday when all packing plants are back on line pushed December up for higher prices the 13th day in a row. Packers closed for the Veterans Day holiday Monday will be needing hogs, traders said.
Fund buying added to gains as did spillover from stronger cattle futures, but prices slipped on commercial profit taking when fund buying subsided, they said.
Rand Financials sold after buying early along with R.J. O'Brien, Dean Witter and Rosenthal Collins in nearbys. Lind-Waldock was a buyer in April early, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock sold December 54 calls and Merrill Lynch bought October 64 calls, pit sources added.
Both markets closed at noon CST in observance of Veterans Day.
